seoTitle: Which Superstore Character Are You? Cloud 9 Superstore Test (12 Questions)
metaDescription: Take the Superstore test: 12 everyday questions reveal whether you're Amy, Jonah, Dina, Glenn, Garrett, Mateo or Cheyenne — with your full character breakdown.
intro: Are you the tired realist holding the whole place together, the idealist who wants to fix the system, or the rule-enforcer with a passion for birds? Answer 12 questions about how you really handle work, customers and coworkers and find out which Superstore character you are.

characters.name: Amy Sosa
characters.title: The Tired Realist
characters.summary: Practical, sarcastic and quietly holding everything together. You've seen it all — and you're very tired of it.
description: Like Amy, you're the one who actually gets things done. She went from floor supervisor to store manager, handling every crisis while everyone else wandered off.
You're a realist. You don't have time for big speeches about changing the world — you've got bills to pay.
But underneath the sarcasm, you want more for your life, and you're braver than you think.
characters.flaw: You're cynical and slow to believe things can get better.
characters.signature: A vest, a walkie-talkie and a very tired sigh.
characters.clashReason: they'd roll their eyes at your big ideas

characters.name: Jonah Simms
characters.title: The Well-Meaning Idealist
characters.summary: Earnest, thoughtful and determined to make things better. You just really want everyone to like you.
description: Like Jonah, you believe things can be better. You'll stand up for your co-workers, fight for fairness and give a speech about it.
You can be a little preachy. Jonah's heart is always in the right place, but he's not always as smooth as he thinks.
And you hate the idea that someone might not like you.
characters.flaw: You're preachy and you need everyone's approval.
characters.signature: A heartfelt speech and a hopeful look at Amy.
characters.clashReason: they'd give a speech when you just need the job done

characters.name: Dina Fox
characters.title: The Intense Rule-Enforcer
characters.summary: Strict, intense and unapologetically yourself. You love rules, authority — and your birds.
description: Like Dina, you take the rules seriously. Very seriously. You enforce them even when your own boss would rather you didn't.
You're intimidating and blunt, and you don't care what anyone thinks of that.
But you're loyal, and there's a surprisingly soft side to you — especially when it comes to birds.
characters.flaw: You're intimidating, and you can be very controlling.
characters.signature: A clipboard, a stern stare and a home full of birds.
characters.clashReason: they'd follow every rule and make you follow them too

characters.name: Glenn Sturgis
characters.title: The Sweet, Naive Boss
characters.summary: Kind, faithful and a little clueless. You see the best in everyone — and you'd do anything for your work family.
description: Like Glenn, you're kind to a fault. He's the store manager and he treats his employees like family, even when they don't deserve it.
Your faith matters to you. Glenn is devoutly religious, and it shapes almost every decision he makes.
You're a little naive and very emotional, but everyone knows you mean well.
characters.flaw: You're naive and easily taken advantage of.
characters.signature: A cardigan, a warm heart and an awkward, well-meaning speech.
characters.clashReason: they'd be nice to the point of exhausting

characters.name: Garrett McNeill
characters.title: The Deadpan Announcer
characters.summary: Laid-back, sarcastic and doing the absolute minimum. You've got the best one-liners in the building.
description: Like Garrett, you're effortlessly cool. He runs the store's announcements, and he uses them to roast everyone.
You don't do more than you have to. Why would you?
But you notice everything, and your deadpan comments are usually the truest thing anyone says all day.
characters.flaw: You're lazy and you'd rather comment on life than take part in it.
characters.signature: A microphone and a perfectly timed, completely unenthusiastic announcement.
characters.clashReason: they'd make fun of everything you care about

characters.name: Mateo Liwanag
characters.title: The Ambitious Diva
characters.summary: Sassy, stylish and extremely ambitious. You want to get to the top — and look fabulous doing it.
description: Like Mateo, you've got big plans. He started at Cloud 9 on the same day as Jonah and immediately started plotting his rise to the top.
You're dramatic and you know it. Your comebacks are sharp, your standards are high, and your gossip is premium.
Underneath the sass, you're a loyal friend who's been through a lot more than people realise.
characters.flaw: You're vain and you can be a little mean.
characters.signature: A perfect outfit and an even more perfect insult.
characters.clashReason: they'd be ambitious enough to walk right over you

characters.name: Cheyenne Lee
characters.title: The Clueless Gossip
characters.summary: Sweet, spacey and somehow knows everybody's business. You're not always following — but you're always fun.
description: Like Cheyenne, you're sweet and a little bit spacey. You say things that make everyone stop and stare.
But you know everything. Cheyenne is the one who somehow always has the gossip on what's going on in the store.
You're younger than most, but you're figuring life out your own way — and you're more capable than people assume.
characters.flaw: You're a bit clueless, and you say whatever's in your head.
characters.signature: A phone, a wild story and a completely unexpected fact.
characters.clashReason: they'd never do anything on time

questions.text: A customer is yelling at you over something that isn't your fault. You...

options.text: Stay calm. You've handled this a thousand times
Nod along and zone out until they leave
Apologise way too much and offer them a free gift
Smile, then roast them the second they leave

questions.text: The power cuts out at work and customers start to panic. You...

options.text: Announce it over the speakers, as calmly as possible
Follow the emergency procedure exactly
Hand out snacks and check everyone's okay
Film it. This is content

questions.text: A promotion opens up at work. You...

options.text: Go for it hard. You've been planning your rise for months
Think about it — then worry you don't want the stress
Want it badly. Finally, someone to keep order around here
Pass. More work for the same pay? No thanks
Nap, snacks and scrolling until it's dark
Brunch, a spa and a lot of photos
The couch. Sports. Don't call
A museum and a documentary, and you'll want to talk about both

questions.text: It's a long, slow shift. How do you get through it?

options.text: Do as little as humanly possible, with style
Hide somewhere quiet and scroll your phone
Start a deep conversation with whoever's nearby
Look for someone breaking the rules

questions.text: A coworker is clearly having a hard time at home. You...

options.text: Invite them over for dinner and treat them like family
Organise a collection for them by the end of the day
Act like you don't care — then quietly help
Tell them the truth they need to hear, kindly-ish
Budget carefully. You've done this before
Still buy the nice skincare. Priorities
Budget? What's a budget?
Give some away anyway, to someone who needs it more

questions.text: Someone at work asks you out. You...

options.text: Say yes, then immediately overthink everything
Turn them down — then think about them all week
Tell them exactly what you expect from a partner. In detail
Play it completely cool

questions.text: Your boss asks you to lead the morning team meeting. You...

options.text: Prepare a heartfelt speech — and get emotional halfway through
Completely forget it was today and wing it
Turn it into a discussion about workers' rights
Use it to show upper management you're ready for more

questions.text: Your workplace announces it's closing for good. You...

options.text: Feel weirdly sad about a place you complained about every day
Make sure everyone has somewhere to go before you think about yourself
Throw everyone the best goodbye party they've ever had
Start applying for new jobs that same day

questions.text: Your coworkers are planning to walk out on strike. If it fails, you could all lose your jobs. You...

options.text: Lead it. Somebody has to stand up to them
Join — but only if there's a real plan
Keep working. Someone has to follow the rules
Sure. A day off is a day off

questions.text: On the busiest sale day of the year, you catch a coworker stealing from the stockroom. They're a single parent and they're really struggling. You...

options.text: Report it. Rules exist for a reason
Pull them aside and warn them. Just this once
Cover for them — and slip them some of your own money
Pretend you saw nothing. Not your business
